No, routine intraoperative frozen-section examination of sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer is not always worthwhile. 

This procedure can help identify patients who require immediate axillary lymph node dissection, but it has limitations, such as false-negative results and the potential for additional surgical time. The American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) recommends against routine use of intraoperative frozen-section examination for sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer, citing the low likelihood of changing the initial surgical management and the potential for additional costs and complications. However, it may be considered in certain situations, such as for patients with large or high-risk tumors, or when the result would change the surgical plan. Ultimately, the decision to perform intraoperative frozen-section examination should be individualized based on patient-specific factors and discussion with the multidisciplinary care team.
